messages:
elaine: Quick thought — we should converge on a tiny ResumeSession primitive across Python/TS/Go to simplify pagination + transport retries. Rough idea: SDK exposes a resume-able iterator that yields pages/items and a resume_token. SDK vs transport decides who persists token. Proposal below.

rashid: +1 to converging. Main Q: are tokens opaque server cursors or client-generated idempotency tokens?

elaine: Short answer: both. Prefer opaque server cursors for correctness (server owns state), but client-generated idempotency tokens help when you want client-driven resume semantics across different transports or if the server cursor expires quickly. I sketched 3 modes: SERVER_CURSOR, CLIENT_TOKEN, HYBRID (server cursor + SDK-provided client token).

sam: Can you paste language sketches for the SDK surface so we can see ergonomics?

elaine: TS sketch:
```ts
// async iterable per-page; page includes optional resumeToken
for await (const page of client.listItems({ q })) {
  for (const it of page.items) { /* handle item */ }
}
// page.resumeToken: string | undefined
```

Python sketch:
```py
# context manager handles background prefetch/connection lifecycle
with client.list_items(q) as stream:
    for page in stream:
        for it in page.items:
            process(it)
# after exit: stream.resume_token -> str | None
```

Go sketch:
```go
// iterator returns (page, token, err). Token is the server/client token for resume.
it := client.ListItems(ctx, params)
for {
  page, token, err := it.Next(ctx)
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { return err }
  // process page.Items
}
```

rashid: I like the shapes. Transport concerns: if SDK prefetches N pages, where is the canonical resume token? If server-provided cursor moves forward, prefetching could make last_token differ from last-delivered item. We should keep the "last acknowledged" token separate from an in-flight token. Also persist via optional callback: on_token(token) so apps can checkpoint.

kevin: Retry semantics need to be clear: transport-level retries are safe for idempotent unary calls. For pagination pages that _consume_ state (server cursor advances), retries are unsafe unless server has idempotency semantics. My suggestion: transport only retries on safe errors (network, idempotent RPC). For recoverable iterator failures, SDK should surface a ResumeableError that includes last_resume_token and the failure reason; app or SDK auto-resume policy can decide.

maria: Could we add an opt-in auto_resume that will attempt resume-with-client-token up to N times with backoff? Default off. Useful for transient infra blips where app wants best-effort continuity. We should emit metrics: resume.attempts, resume.success, resume.failure_reason. :thumbsup:

sam: Ops note: we should record when resume uses client_token vs server_cursor for billing/cost analytics. Also add flags to the trace so we can debug where a resume happened.

elaine: Implementation plan (short):
- RFC: define ResumePolicy enum + error classes (ErrResumeExpired, ResumeableError)
- SDK surfaces: iterator/stream with resume_token attr, optional PersistResumeToken callback, and auto_resume config (off by default)
- Transport: expose optional ResumeHandshake RPC used only in CLIENT_TOKEN mode; transport continues to own low-level retries for idempotent calls
- Docs: migration guide and examples for Python/TS/Go

kevin: Edge cases to call out:
- server cursor expiry -> SDK should surface ErrResumeExpired with last token and a suggested recovery (fresh listing, or restart with client_token)
- partial page delivery (stream cut mid-page) -> SDK should avoid duplicating items when resuming. Need server-side dedupe or stable monotonic offsets in responses.
- cross-lang error model: TS async iterator should throw an error object that includes lastResumeToken; Python should attach resume_token on the exception; Go should return a typed error implementing ResumeInfo() string.

maria: Naming bikeshed: list_items returning an iterator vs list_items_paginator. I prefer keeping the RPC name stable (list_items) and let language SDKs choose the ergonomic surface (sync iterator, async iterator, Next()). Keep helper sugar thin.

ci-bot: "elaine" opened RFC PR 2345: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/2345 (draft) - check it out.

sam: I'll prototype the TS async iterator shape this week and wire a small fake transport that exercises CLIENT_TOKEN + SERVER_CURSOR modes. I'll also add tests for resume token persistence callback.

elaine: Great — I'll iterate on the RFC to include concrete error shapes and the PersistResumeToken API. Owners: elaine (RFC + Python), sam (TS prototype), rashid (Go prototype), kevin (transport retry policy). Target decision: EOW.

maria: Thanks all — feels like a clean, small surface that handles our real-world needs without leaking transport details to app authors.

kevin: +1

elaine: Thanks! I'll ping when PR is ready for review.
